architecture-v1.png.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production texture atlas for original PS Vita pixel-art run-and-gun Iron Coast. Generate a 1536 by 1024 image, exact 3 columns by 2 rows of equal 512x512 SQUARE full-bleed architectural MATERIAL panels, NO gutters NO labels NO text NO outlines separating cells. Each cell is an orthographic front-facing flat wall surface, filling its entire square, no perspective, no sky, no scenery, no characters, no floor. Designed to be sampled as six independent wall textures in a game renderer which adds its own doors/windows/roof/lighting. Top-left: weathered blue-grey harbor warehouse brick with steel vertical structural ribs and subtle rivets. Top-middle: dark desaturated moss-green pump-house corrugated sheet metal. Top-right: navy freight-car ribbed steel with a horizontal seam. Bottom-left: charcoal foundry heat-worn brick and soot-dark iron reinforcement. Bottom-middle: cool grey relay station concrete slabs with thin panel joints. Bottom-right: dark gunmetal command-hangar wall panels with subdued red wear accents. All six consistent realistic pixel-art rendering, crisp deliberate pixel clusters, finely textured but subdued contrast for actors readability, cinematic restrained industrial mood, cool ambient lighting without baked bright lamps. No windows, no doors, no props, no logos. These are original seamless-looking material surfaces, not copies of any existing game.

climb-v2.png.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Reference image only: the original Iron Coast hero Deniz. Create a NEW production animation sprite atlas on a genuinely transparent background, 1024x768, exactly 4 columns and 3 rows of equal 256x256 cells, 12 whole-body poses. Preserve the reference character: black tousled hair, brass goggles on head, teal scarf, dark sleeveless shirt, ochre cargo pants, brown boots, small utility backpack. Same detailed crisp pixel art and proportions. Character faces AWAY from camera, climbing a vertical ladder with both hands, weapon strapped on back, but DO NOT DRAW THE LADDER. First two rows: eight sequential alternating-arm alternating-leg ladder climbing poses forming a loop, visible boot soles and bent knees, careful in-between poses, all body sizes identical, centered x in each cell, lowest boot at y=224 in each cell, full body contained within x=60..196 and y=32..224; keep each pose safely separated from neighbors. Last row: four transition poses: reaching to grab ladder from standing, pulling hips onto top ledge, crouching at top to descend, releasing ladder to stand. No labels, numbers, grid lines, shadows on background, props, repeated checkerboard, or other characters. Exact equal cell layout and consistent body scale are critical to prevent animation mapping errors.
